questions.def: Reflexive pronoun needed because they helped 'them'.
questions.question: They helped ___ to some food.

questions.def: 'Herself' is the reflexive pronoun for 'she'.
questions.question: She bought ___ a new dress.

questions.def: 'Yourself' is the reflexive pronoun to complete the phrase.
questions.question: Did you ___ at the party?

questions.def: Reflexive pronoun needed because we made it for 'us'.
questions.question: We made ___ some coffee.

questions.def: 'Himself' is the reflexive pronoun for 'he'.
questions.question: He cut ___ while cooking.

questions.def: 'Yourself' is used for a singular, informal invitation.
questions.question: Please ___ to the cake.

questions.def: 'Itself' is the reflexive pronoun for animals (it).
questions.question: The cat cleaned ___.

questions.def: 'Themselves' is the reflexive pronoun for 'they'.
questions.question: They blamed ___ for the mistake.

questions.def: 'Myself' is the reflexive pronoun used after 'me'.
questions.question: Let me ___.

questions.def: 'Ourselves' refers back to 'we'.
questions.question: We should trust ___ more.

questions.def: 'Himself' is the reflexive pronoun for 'he'.
questions.question: He prides ___ on his cooking skills.

questions.def: 'Themselves' because the subject is plural 'kids'.
questions.question: The kids didn't ___.

questions.def: 'Each other' is used when two people are interacting.
questions.question: They often argue with ___.

questions.def: 'One another' is used for more than two people.
questions.question: The students helped ___ with the project.

questions.def: 'Each other' is used when two people perform an action.
questions.question: The two friends ___ last week.

questions.def: 'One another' is used when more than two interact.
questions.question: The team members supported ___ during the competition.

questions.def: 'Each other' is used when only two people interact.
questions.question: The two sisters love ___ very much.

questions.def: 'Each other' because they mutually met.
questions.question: They ___ at the party.

questions.def: Each other is the correct reciprocal pronoun to use.
questions.question: The twins look like ___.

questions.def: 'One another' is used when there are more than two involved.
questions.question: The football players congratulated ___ after the game.

questions.def: 'One another' implies that there were more than two classmates.
questions.question: The classmates ___ .

questions.def: 'Yourself' is the reflexive form of 'you' (singular).
questions.question: Please don't blame ___.

questions.def: 'Themselves' is the correct reflexive pronoun for 'children'.
questions.question: The children are old enough to dress ___.

questions.def: Use 'themselves' when the subject (they) performs and receives the action.
questions.question: They helped ___ with the project.

questions.def: Use 'herself' because the subject 'she' is female and singular.
questions.question: She looked at ___ in the mirror.

questions.def: 'Enjoy' needs a reflexive pronoun when the subject is the receiver of the action.
questions.question: We ___ the party very much.

questions.def: Use 'yourself' when addressing someone directly (you).
questions.question: Did you hurt ___?

questions.def: 'Each other' indicates a reciprocal action between two people.
questions.question: They often help ___.

questions.def: They introduced THEMSELVES (reflexive) or each other (reciprocal).
questions.question: They ___ at the meeting.

questions.def: 'Ourselves' is the reflexive pronoun for 'we'.
questions.question: We made the cake ___.
